solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Expedition to find source of water in desert (8)

indicators.note: the spring goes in the desert-word

blocks.note: to ditch = to desert, abandon
a spa is a mineral spring

annotation.surface: An explorer sets out across the dunes hoping to find a spring.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desert' reads as a noun, a sandy place, but it is the verb: to desert someone is to DITCH them. Expedition here is speed, not a journey.
annotation.definitionFit: Dispatch and expedition both mean promptness in getting something done.

clue.text: Blood group of singers displays elevated iodine (5)

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting the I moves it up to the top

blocks.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine
CHOIR, with its I lifted out to go on top

annotation.surface: A choir shows off its members' blood types and a raised iodine reading, like a medical report.
annotation.walkthrough: CHOIR already holds every letter; the clue only moves its I from fourth place to first, which in a down entry is raising it.
annotation.definitionFit: Ichor is the ethereal fluid that ran in the veins of the Greek gods in place of blood.

clue.text: Precipitate crisis in migration, carried out by people like this (11)

definitions.text: in migration, carried out by people like this

indicators.note: a crisis throws the letters of PRECIPITATE into turmoil

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters, the same letters as the answer

annotation.surface: A news line about something sparking a migration crisis.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Precipitate' looks like the verb (to bring on a crisis), but it is only a bag of letters. The definition is descriptive: people who migrate are peripatetic.
annotation.definitionFit: Peripatetic means travelling from place to place, which is how migrating people live.

clue.text: Contracts bug visiting contests (8)

indicators.note: a visitor is inside the house, so EAT goes inside TRIES

blocks.note: tries = trials, contests of strength or skill
to bug = to eat at, annoy: 'what's eating you?'

annotation.surface: An insect wanders into a sporting competition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bug' suggests an insect or a listening device; here it is the verb to annoy, as in 'what's eating you?'.
annotation.definitionFit: Treaties are formal contracts between states.

clue.text: Ginger Ron and her team magically vanquishing Voldemort at last! (15)

definitions.text: Ginger Ron and her team magically vanquishing Voldemort at last!

indicators.note: by magic the letters rearrange themselves
vanquishing the last letter of Voldemort defeats T and removes it from TEAM

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder
TEAM with its T removed
the last letter of Voldemort, the letter taken away

annotation.surface: A Harry Potter moment: ginger-haired Ron and his friend's team finally beat Voldemort with magic.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: Hermione, Ron and Harry together defeat Voldemort in the last book. The 'and' only joins her to Ron in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: read straight, the whole clue describes the witch who, with red-haired Ron Weasley and Harry, brings about Voldemort's final defeat.

clue.text: Censor Communist legislation (6)

blocks.note: red is the colour of communism
an act of parliament is a piece of legislation

annotation.surface: A censor at work in a communist state, blacking out the laws.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: redacting is exactly what a communist censor does to documents.
annotation.definitionFit: To redact a document is to censor it by blacking out parts.

clue.text: Aware sceptre has handle (6)

indicators.note: the sceptre-word holds USE inside it

blocks.note: a sceptre is a ceremonial rod
to handle = to use

annotation.surface: A monarch's sceptre with a handle on it, oddly described as alert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a noun that a sceptre would have, but it is the verb, to USE.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone roused from sleep is awake and aware.

clue.text: Bomb which gets shaken and then thrown (3)

definitions.text: which gets shaken and then thrown

blocks.note: the verb for a show or joke failing badly with an audience

blocks.clueFragment: which gets shaken and then thrown
blocks.note: the numbered cube rattled in the hand before a board-game move

annotation.surface: A bomb that gets shaken before being hurled.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a grenade; in fact a show that bombs dies on stage, and a die is the cube you shake and throw in board games.
annotation.definitionFit: To bomb is to fail badly, which is to die; a die is one of a pair of dice.

clue.text: In bed, teased holding tip of bay leaf (9)

indicators.note: the bed-and-teased string holds the Y inside it

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
the tip, or end, of BAY is Y
to lead someone on = to tease them

annotation.surface: Someone in bed being teased with a bay leaf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tip of bay' tempts you to take B, but there is no B in the answer: the tip here is the end letter, Y. 'Bay leaf' also looks like one phrase but splits.
annotation.definitionFit: A cotyledon is a seed leaf, the first leaf to appear from a germinating seed.

clue.text: Order tax raid (6)

blocks.note: the verb for commanding someone to do something
a fee or levy imposed on someone
a headlong rush on the enemy, as cavalry make

annotation.surface: An instruction to carry out a raid on the taxman.
annotation.walkthrough: This is really three definitions in three words: to charge is to order, a charge is a tax or fee, and a charge is an attack.
annotation.definitionFit: Charge can mean a command, a fee levied, and a headlong attack.

clue.text: Spin this wheel when blockage is in road (8)

indicators.note: the blockage sits inside the road

blocks.note: a route is a road
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

annotation.surface: Advice to take your chances at the wheel when the road is blocked.
annotation.walkthrough: LET as an obstruction survives in legal phrasing and in tennis, where a let is a serve that is obstructed by the net.
annotation.definitionFit: The roulette wheel is spun in a casino game of chance.

clue.text: End of film clip broadcast (4)

indicators.note: on air we hear the word, not see its spelling

blocks.note: a clip or rap is a sharp blow

annotation.surface: The last scene of a film being shown as a clip on television.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clip' suggests a film excerpt, fitting the surface, but it is a smack round the ear: a rap.
annotation.definitionFit: 'It's a wrap' is called when filming is finished, so a wrap is the end of shooting.

clue.text: Thread with online agitator is necessary for one’s business (6,4)

blocks.note: toile is a linen or cotton cloth, loosely thread
a troll posts to provoke people online

annotation.surface: A discussion thread with a troll in it, as if trolls were essential to trade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thread' and 'online agitator' set up an internet forum, and 'business' sounds commercial; it is the euphemism for going to the lavatory.
annotation.definitionFit: Toilet roll is the essential supply when you do your business in the loo.

clue.text: Apart from one litre, I sell Arabian refined crude (11)

indicators.note: 'apart from' means excluding, so one L is set aside from the letters that follow
refining processes the letters into a new form

blocks.note: L = litre; one of the two Ls in the fodder goes
I SELL ARABIAN less one L, anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: An oil trader offering Arabian crude, refined, at the pump.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Refined' and 'crude' are both oil words and seem opposed; crude is the definition, in its sense of vulgar.
annotation.definitionFit: Rabelaisian means coarsely, bawdily humorous, after the French writer Rabelais.

clue.text: Temple to Leopard King is scratched on (8)

indicators.note: scratched from the list, so R is removed

blocks.note: PANTHER, a leopard, without its R
R = rex, king; the letter removed
on stays as itself

annotation.surface: A temple dedicated to a leopard king with an inscription scratched on it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scratched' looks like carving, but it means withdrawn, as a horse is scratched from a race.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Pantheon in Rome was built as a shrine to every god, and the word now also names any building honouring the great.

clue.text: Software supported by big bet on good and evil (9)

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of what supports it
G is placed next to the bet

blocks.note: an app is a piece of software
going all in is staking everything
G = good

annotation.surface: A gambling app lets you place huge bets on the battle of good and evil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good and evil' reads as one phrase, but 'good' is only a G and 'evil' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Something appalling is shockingly bad, which is close to evil.

clue.text: Young man takes vitamin for physique (4)

indicators.note: the young man takes D inside himself

blocks.note: a boy is a young man
vitamin D

annotation.surface: A young man takes vitamin supplements to build his physique.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a gym-goer's routine, and it fits the answer: that is exactly why he takes vitamins.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: physique means the build and shape of a person, as in 'a swimmer's body'.

clue.text: Inspector Morse’s baffled by idiot losing murderer’s head (8)

indicators.note: baffled letters are confused and jumbled
lose the head, the first letter, of murderer

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
MORSES without its M, anagram fodder
the first letter of murderer, removed

annotation.surface: Inspector Morse, the TV detective, is stumped by a fool while the killer stays hidden.
annotation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a British television detective, so 'Inspector Morse' looks like one name; 'Inspector' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An assessor inspects and evaluates, for tax or insurance claims.

clue.text: Did hawk flip over bugs? (4)

indicators.note: flipping turns the word end to end

blocks.note: to bug a phone is to tap it

annotation.surface: A hawk tumbling in the air after catching insects.
annotation.walkthrough: The hawk is a verb: to hawk is to clear the throat and spit, so 'did hawk' is SPAT. The bugs are wiretaps, not insects.
annotation.definitionFit: Spat is the past tense of spit, which is what someone who hawks does.

clue.text: Petrol’s ultimately contaminating poor sealion (8)

indicators.note: take the ultimate, final letter of contaminating
a poor sealion is in a bad way, its letters in a mess

blocks.note: the last letter of contaminating
SEALION rearranged

annotation.surface: An oil spill poisoning a sea lion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Petrol’s ultimately' looks like it should give S, the end of petrol; the 's is a link meaning 'is', and it is 'contaminating' that gets cut to its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: what the British call petrol, Americans call by this longer name, usually shortened to gas.

clue.text: Unstable jetty has centre that is not straight (6)

indicators.note: the jetty has BI at its centre

blocks.note: a mole is a stone pier or breakwater
bi = bisexual, not straight

annotation.surface: A wobbly jetty whose middle section has warped.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That is' tempts you to write IE; the whole phrase 'that is not straight' describes BI.
annotation.definitionFit: Something mobile moves easily, so it is not fixed or stable.

clue.text: They pick leaders of opposition, legislature, etcetera, at random (10)

indicators.note: take the leading letters of opposition and legislature
the letters come out in no set order

blocks.note: first letters of opposition and legislature
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A complaint that voters choose party leaders and politicians with no rhyme or reason.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface and the answer share a scene: the electorate do pick the opposition and the legislature.
annotation.definitionFit: The electorate are the voters, those who pick who governs.

clue.text: Assassinated: chopped head off (4)

indicators.note: a word with its head taken off has lost its first letter, as a beheaded body loses its top

blocks.note: DICED, chopped into cubes, without its D

annotation.surface: A grisly report of an assassination by beheading.
annotation.walkthrough: To ice someone is gangster slang for killing them. Chopped here is diced, in the kitchen sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: in gangster talk, putting someone on ice means killing them, so an assassinated target has been dealt with this way.

clue.text: Dispenses drug to Cambridge University student head (5)

indicators.note: the head of student is its first letter

blocks.note: E = ecstasy
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts
first letter of student

annotation.surface: A dealer supplying drugs to a student at Cambridge.
annotation.walkthrough: Cambridge University looks English, but the Cambridge here is in Massachusetts, home of MIT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean giving something out, as a machine dispenses tickets or a chimney sends out smoke.

clue.text: Chewing gaudy decoration on top of pen? (8)

indicators.note: in an across answer, the decoration goes after the nib

blocks.note: the nib is the writing tip of a pen
bling is flashy jewellery

annotation.surface: Someone chewing a pen with a flashy decoration on its cap.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a person chewing a fancy pen, which is apt: nibbling a pen is a familiar habit.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: taking small repeated bites is a gentle form of chewing, the way a mouse works at cheese.

clue.text: Surprise ending cut from novel (3)

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: BOOK, a novel, without its K

annotation.surface: A novel with a twist ending that got edited out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Surprise ending' reads as a plot twist; 'Surprise' is the definition, and 'ending cut' works on the book.
annotation.definitionFit: Boo! is what you say to surprise someone.

clue.text: Topples over after imbibing one alcoholic drink (6)

indicators.note: turned over, so TRIPS runs backwards
having drunk the I, the word holds it inside

blocks.note: TRIPS, topples, turned over
I = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A drinker falls over after downing one drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a drunk toppling after one spirit; TRIPS is the word for topples, turned over.
annotation.definitionFit: Spirits such as gin and whisky are strong alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Miss and Mr (in Italy, but not Sweden) (6)

indicators.note: take the Italian title without S

blocks.note: SIGNORE, Italian for Mr, without the S
S is the international car code for Sweden

annotation.surface: Forms of address in Italy, as if listing titles by country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Miss and Mr' look like a pair of titles; Miss is the verb, to ignore.
annotation.definitionFit: To miss something is to fail to notice it, to ignore it.

clue.text: In Meissen era, repairs reflected scarce quality (8)

indicators.note: the answer is inside these words
seen in a mirror, it reads backwards

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of Meissen across 'era' to the first letter of repairs

annotation.surface: Restoring Meissen porcelain of a certain period, a rare skill.
annotation.walkthrough: Meissen is a German porcelain maker, so the surface is about antiques; the answer runs backwards across 'MeisSEN ERA, Repairs'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain definition: the -NESS ending names a quality, and rare means scarce.
